Claim: 'Almost half a million in verified profits in the last 12 trading days' across ~20+ prop accounts.
Evidence type: Screen-share of broker dashboards during a live webinar + verbal attestation by Rob Hoffman (WealthCharts CEO) at 53:43: 'I had my guys stop in at $375,000 ... I can verify you did those trades'
Visible denominator: NO - no account count, no starting balance, no losing days, no trade count
Costs included: NO - prop evaluation fees, resets and platform costs not netted
Independently verified: NO - the attesting party is the commercial partner whose product is being sold in the same broadcast
Assessment: Selected highlight; creator-reported with partner attestation. Not an audited record. The attestation covers 'these trades happened', not 'this is the full result of the strategy'.
Relevance: Does not establish expectancy. Must not be used to justify testing any parameter.

Claim: '$61,000 P&L, 82% win rate. 92% win rate. 90% win rate on Apex'
Assessment: Selected highlight, three different numbers in one breath, no definition of what the percentage counts (trades? days? accounts?)
Relevance: None.

Claim: 'I haven't had a red day since I've used wealth charts.'
Assessment: Marketing claim made immediately after a sponsor plug; immediately qualified by 'I'm not saying that's going to happen to you'.
Relevance: None.

Claim: 'I'm up almost 70,000 in payouts this month' / '40,000 on the day' / '58,000 in funded profits'
Assessment: Creator-reported, selected day.
Relevance: None.

Claim: Live $3,000 payout request shown on screen and approved.
Assessment: This is the STRONGEST single piece of performance evidence found: a contemporaneous, on-screen payout request. It still proves only that one payout occurred.
Relevance: Weakly supportive that the operator is genuinely trading funded accounts. Says nothing about strategy expectancy.

Claim: 'I think I'm on 45 Midgard accounts and at least 200 trade[s] ... I'd be blowing accounts like the [rest]. I'm one of us.'
Assessment: Volunteered negative disclosure. Materially undercuts CL-001 to CL-004: the denominator includes many blown accounts.
Relevance: HIGH relevance - this is the only quantitative hint at the denominator, and it is large.

Claim: '28 of my last 28 accounts funded using one strategy surrounded about that orb' and 'over 25 payouts'.
Assessment: Unsupported. Directly contradicted by CL-006 from a later video.
Relevance: None, except as a contradiction marker.

Claim: 'I invented a strategy that has a 91% success rate with orb ... I'm not going to give you guys the secret sauce, it's going to be in my Mastermind.'
Assessment: Unverifiable by construction. The claim is used as the hook for a $1,997 product sold later in the same broadcast (V8 45:15).
Relevance: None for testing. Relevant only as evidence that the highest-claimed variant is NOT in the public material.

Claim: Video title: 'Trading Strategy With 92% Success Rate'.
Assessment: Title claim. Not reviewed; recorded for completeness only.
Relevance: None.

Claim: '18 straight green days' and 'three accounts ... I haven't had a red trade yet'.
Assessment: Selected highlight from ~2 years ago on evaluation accounts.
Relevance: None.

Claim: MVG indicator: '99% of gaps get filled, 86% of them get filled in the same day'; 'if you were to trade the max value gap alone, you'd be 24 for 28 right now. An 85% win rate.'
Visible denominator: Partial - '24 for 28' has a denominator but no period, symbol or rule definition
Assessment: Vendor-generated statistic for a product being launched in the same broadcast. Gap-fill percentages of this magnitude are trivially inflatable by choosing a small gap definition and an unbounded time horizon.
Relevance: Not part of the ORB families. Flagged because it may be offered later as a filter - it should not be adopted without an independent test.

Claim: 'ORB works best on large move mornings and days ... when you do the large statistical data'.
Assessment: Unsupported assertion referencing private analysis.
Relevance: HIGH relevance as a HYPOTHESIS: it is objectively testable (condition ORB performance on opening-range width or on realised morning volatility) and it is the only conditioning variable Max ever names. Recommend the Analyst test it.

Claim: 'ORB has been in the markets for 40 years / this was named 60 years ago. I did not invent this. I just made it mainstream.'
Independently verified: Partially - ORB is genuinely a long-standing published concept (Crabel et al.), so the historical part is broadly accurate
Assessment: Honest attribution. Notable because it is the one place he disclaims originality.
Relevance: Context only.

Claim: 'Statistically on Fridays ... if you look at 20 years worth of data, Fridays give the cleanest trends out of any day in the market.'
Assessment: Unsupported. Testable.
Relevance: Testable day-of-week hypothesis. Low priority.

Claim: '$315,000 last year in prop accounts, cash and charity giveaways'; '$259,000 in free accounts this year'.
Assessment: Marketing / community claim. Not a performance claim.
Relevance: None.

Claim: 'Over $3 million of options trading'.
Assessment: Unsupported.
Relevance: None.

Claim: Affiliate and commercial relationships are pervasive and disclosed only as promo codes, not as material-connection disclosures.
Assessment: Apex (BDM / BIGDADDY90), WealthCharts (BIGDADDY90), Tradeify, Alpha Futures (BDM), My Funded Futures (MAXORB), Funded Next (BDM), plus his own course, Mastermind and indicator suite. Every webinar reviewed is co-branded with a platform or prop firm and ends in a discount code.
Relevance: HIGH relevance to evidence weighting: the instructional videos are sales vehicles. Chart examples are selected to sell. This is a reason to weight LIVE sessions above webinar teardowns when judging what he actually does.

Claim: 'I've never back tested a day in my life. Ever. I forward test.'
Evidence type: Creator statement, in direct answer to an audience question
Assessment: Volunteered and credible. It is NOT a performance claim - it is a methodology disclosure, and it bears directly on CL-012 and CL-014.
Relevance: HIGH. CL-012 ('when you do the large statistical data, ORB works best on large move mornings') and CL-014 ('20 years worth of data' on Fridays) both appeal to statistical work. CL-018 says he has never done any. Treat both as impressions, not findings.

Claim: 'I rock a 90.5% success rate right here team. 90.5.'
Assessment: Unsupported. A fourth distinct win-rate figure (cf. 82/92/90 in CL-002, 91% in CL-008).
Relevance: None.

Claim: Advanced ORB indicator: 'Identify the opening range high/low and catch high-momentum breakouts in the first hour of trade.' Indicator suite from $30/week.
Assessment: No opening-range definition, no breakout-vs-reversal logic, no entry/stop/target rule and no source are published. NOT INSPECTABLE WITHOUT PURCHASE; not purchased.
Relevance: Answers RR-002 Q1 item 3: U-01 cannot be settled from the indicator.

Claim: 'There's an 85 to 87% chance of success if you break orb and previous day highs or lows at the same time.'
Evidence type: Creator statement over a daily NQ chart
Assessment: No denominator, no definition of 'success', no period. BUT it is falsifiable and specific — the only testable number he has ever given.
Relevance: HIGH as a test target. A claimed 85-87% against a measured ~51% base rate is a large enough gap to be worth closing on the record. Gross-first.

Claim: 'I've gone 82 days once without a red trade ... and got banned from that prop firm for rinsing them.'
Assessment: Unverifiable. The ban detail is unfalsifiable as stated.
Relevance: None.

Claim: 'I made $15,000 last month. It's not a great month for me, but I'm proud as hell of it.'
Assessment: MATERIALLY LOWER than every other figure in the corpus ($30k/month CL-001 era, $70k in payouts CL-004, $40k in a day). Volunteered, and it cuts against his own marketing.
Relevance: HIGH. Raises the credibility of the volunteered disclosures and lowers the credibility of the headline numbers.

Claim: Biggest loss: Costco earnings, '$139,000 in 5 seconds', then $30,000 more — 'I blew $169,000 in quite literally about 5 minutes'; Robinhood account 200k to 60k.
Assessment: Volunteered loss disclosure. Options, overnight, earnings event. Consistent with CL-006.
Relevance: Context. Shows the tail risk sits in the options book, not the ORB futures book.

Claim: 'thousands of percent better chance of success' opening at 3:59pm and closing at 9:31 versus holding 9:31 to 3:59.
Assessment: Directionally consistent with a real, well-documented overnight-versus-intraday return asymmetry in equity indices. The stated magnitude is not meaningful.
Relevance: Out of scope for this project, but noted: an overnight hold has one round trip against a much larger move — a different cost geometry from the one that closed every candidate here.

Claim: 'I'm pretty sure I invented this [the MVG].'
Assessment: Not supportable. The construct is a standard price imbalance and the stated mechanism (data-feed lag) is incorrect — see R-056.
Relevance: Credibility marker.
